subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@nordbank.de>, Lukas Fischer <lukas.fischer@nordbank.de>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 14:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode / data residency

Hi Anna / Lukas,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and a few clarification questions so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC / on-prem):

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: embed LLM features into Nordbank customer support workflows with strict EU data residency and low latency to DE/NL regions.
- Usage profile: batch inference for conversation summaries + low-latency chat for agents during office hours (~100k tokens/day to start, growth expected).
- Security/regulatory: GDPR + internal audit controls, potential SOC 2 evidence requests.

Clarification/questions to confirm recommended path:
1) Data residency requirement: do you require data to remain physically within EU (and specifically Germany), or is EU region (e.g., germany-west/europe-west) sufficient?
2) Network preference: would you prefer a Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC / peering) or are you open to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) hosted in an EU region with contractual data residency guarantees?
3) Latency SLO: target 95th pct latency for chat API? (ballpark number helps us size dedicated pools).
4) Procurement timeline / SOW constraints — any deadlines we should be aware of?

Attachments: attaching our EU data residency datasheet and a short questionnaire that helps us recommend Dedicated vs Private.

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus to follow up with region availability and rough sizing based on answers above.
- Quick technical demo (30m) with your infra/arch team to show routing, VPC options, and fallback behavior.

Available times for the demo: Thu 3/26 afternoon CET or Mon 3/30 — happy to work around your schedule.

Best,

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers to help you size / recommend:

1) Data residency: we need all customer data and request/response logs to remain within the EU. Ideally we would like Germany (DE) physical residency, but for initial discussions "EU-only" (europe-west / europe-central) is acceptable if you can confirm no cross-border (non-EU) backups or processing.
2) Network: given our security team and procurement, we expect to move toward a Private VPC (peered) or an on-prem appliance for production. That said, Dedicated reserved capacity in an EU region could work for non-sensitive workloads — we want to understand the differences and the migration path.
3) Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for agent-assist chat would be ideal.
4) Procurement timeline: procurement kickoff next month; target go-live for pilot in Q3. We'll need typical security docs (SOC 2, DPA, encryption at rest/in transit).

Please loop in whoever will cover technical VPC details. Also can you confirm whether Redwood supports cross-region routing / failover in the EU without crossing into the US?

Thanks,
Anna

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 13:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode / data residency

Hi Anna — thanks for the quick responses and helpful constraints. A few technical notes to answer your questions: 

- EU-only residency: we can guarantee that production request processing and persistent logs remain in EU regions (we operate multiple EU regions including germany-west and europe-west). Backups and replication are configurable — they can be restricted to EU regions only. For strict Germany-only residency, our Private (VPC / on-prem) option is the clearest path; Dedicated in germany-west is available for some customers via reserved pools (we should validate capacity for your timeline).

- Private VPC vs Dedicated:
  - Private VPC: customer-managed networking (VPC peering/PrivateLink), full control over egress, recommended for regulated workloads and when you need Germany-only physical residency. Requires longer lead time for network setup and procurement (SLA + connectivity).
  - Dedicated reserved capacity: Redwood manages the serving runtime in an EU region dedicated to your tenant. Faster onboarding (~2–4 weeks), predictably-sized GPU pools, contractual data residency guarantees. Slightly less network isolation than VPC peering, but we provide IP allowlists and private connectivity options in many cases.

- Cross-region routing / failover: yes — we support routing policies that constrain traffic to EU regions. Failover can be configured to an alternate EU region. We will not route traffic through US data centers unless explicitly configured for cost/perf reasons.

- Security artifacts: we can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, DPA template, encryption attestations, and red-team results. Laura (cc'd) will take point on providing evidence.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical demo focused on VPC and Dedicated options (30m) — propose Thu 3/26 16:00 CET or Mon 3/30 10:00 CET.
2) Laura to share SOC2 + DPA drafts and a short runbook describing region constraints and networking options.
3) Marissa to provide a short statement of expected daily tokens and peak concurrency for sizing.

If pilot target is Q3, I'd recommend starting the procurement conversations now so we can lock region capacity.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
